summary: BA's M1 milestone scoping is defensible and the harness/policy schema design is sound. However, the affected-files list is materially incomplete in two specific ways that the spec itself names verbatim, and one significant out-of-scope observation is missing. (1) Spec §5.1 line 90 enumerates seven additional banned agents (`ba`, `qa`, `dev`, `pm`, `product-owner`, `ui-specialist`, `user`) that BA acknowledges in Edge Cases as also requiring the DO-NOT block 'for documentation parity', but then omits from the affected-files list. (2) `/root/travel-planner/scripts/fetch-images-batch.py` makes direct REST calls to `restapi.amap.com` using `AMAP_MAPS_API_KEY` env var (lines 154-158, 395-436, etc.) and shells out to the gaode poi_search.py script — this is a significant code-level gaode reference NOT mentioned in BA's out-of-scope observations. (3) `/root/travel-planner/.claude/commands/plan.md` contains 9+ positive instructions to use gaode-maps (lines 100, 397, 417, 423, 1103, 1144, 1577, 1641, 1673) — orchestrator-level prompt that will become contradictory with the harness ban. Not in BA's affected-files list, not in out-of-scope observations. These omissions are documentation/scope gaps that dev needs explicit guidance on; either the affected-files list expands or BA must explicitly justify omission in writing. Other dimensions (evidence quality on cited line numbers, specialist alignment on single-hook design, AC testability, alias canonicalization rationale) verify cleanly.

The 6 user-level agent files (ba, qa, dev, pm, product-owner, ui-specialist) — which spec §5.1 line 90 enumerates verbatim as 'Out-of-scope agents (must be banned)' — are NOT in the affected-files list.

BA's Edge Cases section explicitly recognizes the gap: 'Recommendation: add the DO-NOT block to ALL non-allowlist agent .md files for documentation parity; let the harness be the actual enforcement.' But the affected-files list (line 217-229 of ticket) does NOT include them. Verified by `ls /root/.claude/agents/`: ba.md, dev.md, pm.md, product-owner.md, qa.md, ui-specialist.md all exist as user-level agent files. user.md also exists.
objections.why_it_matters: Either (a) BA expands affected-files to include the 6+1 user-level agents (consistent with spec verbatim and BA's own Edge Cases recommendation), OR (b) BA explicitly documents in scope_excluded with a written rationale why the user-level agents are out-of-scope for M1 (e.g., 'these are infrastructure agents that structurally cannot reach travel-planner gaode invocations and the harness default-deny suffices'). Currently the ticket has neither: the spec demands them, BA admits the gap, but the affected-files list silently excludes them. Dev cannot tell whether to touch them or not.
objections.required_fix: Add an explicit decision in scope_boundary OR affected_files: either (1) include /root/.claude/agents/{ba,qa,dev,pm,product-owner,ui-specialist,user}.md in the modify list with the DO-NOT block, OR (2) add a paragraph under scope.excluded explicitly naming each of these 7 user-level agent files and writing the rationale (default-deny by harness; documentation parity deferred to M5 or out of project scope). Either resolution is acceptable; ambiguity is not.

objections.summary: Out-of-scope observations missed `scripts/fetch-images-batch.py` (direct gaode REST + script invocation in user code)
objections.ba_claim: BA's out_of_scope_observations lists 4 items: save_translate.py (data-layer tagging), gaode-maps/scripts/*.py (bannable scripts not modified), skills/gaode-maps/skill.md (user-invocable preserved), CLAUDE.md (auto-inventory). Claims the search was thorough.
objections.evidence: Grep `(gaode|amap|高德)` in `/root/travel-planner/scripts/` returns: fetch-images-batch.py:63 invokes .claude/commands/scripts/gaode-maps/scripts/poi_search.py via subprocess; fetch-images-batch.py:154-158 builds `https://restapi.amap.com/v3/geocode/geo` URL directly using `AMAP_MAPS_API_KEY` env var; fetch-images-batch.py:395 has a `_gaode_search` method; lines 410, 436, 509, 514, 564, 568, 1078, 1089 reference gaode in image-fetching logic. This script is invoked by the user (not a subagent) for image enrichment, but it shells out to the same poi_search.py and ALSO calls amap REST directly — both surfaces the new policy explicitly bans for non-allowlist agents.
objections.why_it_matters: (a) If a banned subagent (e.g., images agent if one is added later, or current pipeline shelling) ever invokes `python3 scripts/fetch-images-batch.py`, the script internally calls gaode but the harness only inspects the outer Bash command. The bash-token matcher would not match `fetch-images-batch.py` (no gaode token in the wrapper command) — only the bash-resolved-path matcher would, and `fetch-images-batch.py` does NOT live under a gaode prefix. Result: a banned agent could invoke gaode transitively via this wrapper, defeating the ban. (b) The script ITSELF reads AMAP_KEY env var and POSTs to amap REST — if a banned agent ever runs it, the agent_id-keyed policy doesn't catch the in-process gaode call. BA must either (i) add this script to the affected-files list to block subagent invocation, (ii) document it as a known coverage gap in out_of_scope_observations with security_relevant=true, or (iii) explicitly note that the script is user-invoked-only (no subagent currently invokes it) — each of which is a legitimate posture but ABSENT from the BA spec.
objections.required_fix: Add a 5th out-of-scope observation entry naming /root/travel-planner/scripts/fetch-images-batch.py with line numbers, classifying as in_user_path=false (since user-invoked, not subagent-invoked today), security_relevant=true (because it would be a transit-via-wrapper bypass for the gaode ban if any subagent ever calls it). Optionally extend gaode_denied_bash_resolved_path_prefixes or add a new gaode_denied_bash_token entry for `fetch-images-batch.py` if BA judges the bypass risk warrants harness coverage in M1. At minimum: document the gap so dev does not silently inherit a hole.

objections.summary: Out-of-scope observations missed `.claude/commands/plan.md` (9+ orchestrator-level positive gaode instructions)
objections.ba_claim: BA's out_of_scope_observations does not mention plan.md. The affected-files list includes 7 agent .md files but no command files.
objections.evidence: Grep `(gaode|amap|高德)` in /root/travel-planner/.claude/commands/ returns plan.md:100,397,417,423,1103,1144,1577,1641,1673 — all positive instructions to the orchestrator like 'Agent researches using gaode-maps/rednote', 'use gaode-maps (China) or google-maps (international) to obtain GPS coordinates', 'use MCP tools (gaode-maps, google-maps, rednote) and update working files', 'NEVER use WebSearch, WebFetch, or gaode-maps MCP tools yourself'. plan.md is the /plan slash-command entrypoint that orchestrates the entire travel-planning flow. After M1 lands, the orchestrator's own prompt will say 'tell content agents to use gaode-maps' while the harness blocks them — this is a direct contradiction that surfaces as immediate runtime failure on the next /plan invocation.
objections.why_it_matters: Spec §5.1 second clause: '在 prompt 中也禁止' (also forbid in prompts). This is plural — 'prompts' includes orchestrator prompts that instruct subagent behavior, not just the subagent .md files. BA's M2 outline (Future Cycles) says plan.md is rewritten in M2 ('plan.md inverted to content (multi-option) → user-review → timeline → transportation'), so M2 will naturally rewrite these — but M1 ships and the orchestrator's prompt still actively instructs gaode invocation by banned agents. The 'consistency' between harness and prompt is broken FOR THE M1 WINDOW. Either: (a) M1 is incomplete until plan.md's positive gaode instructions are also updated (or at minimum gated with a 'pending M2' note), or (b) BA explicitly documents this as a known M1→M2 inconsistency window.
objections.required_fix: Add either: (1) plan.md to affected_files with a focused edit removing the 9 positive gaode instructions to non-allowlist agents (preserve mentions only where they reference timeline/transportation); OR (2) an out_of_scope_observation entry naming plan.md:100,397,417,423,1103,1144,1577,1641,1673 with the explicit note 'M1 ships with the orchestrator prompt instructing gaode invocation by banned agents; the harness will block, producing runtime denials on /plan invocation between M1 close and M2 close. M2 rewrites plan.md per Future Cycles outline.' The second option is acceptable IF BA confirms the orchestrator's deny output is interpretable by the user (not a silent hang). The first option is preferable because spec §5.1 clause 2 demands prompt-layer consistency.

Without disambiguation, dev might delete the schema reference and break the output schema validators downstream.

objections.summary: AC2's bash-token check needs the FULL command string, but existing `_extract_targets()` returns only WRITE paths for Bash — implementation pitfall not flagged
objections.ba_claim: BA Technical Hints line 220: 'extend `_extract_targets` to surface-classify; insert `is_gaode_allowed` call BEFORE standard `is_allowed`'. AC2: 'hook exits 2 with surface: bash-token (matched on gaode-maps/)'.
objections.evidence: Read of /root/.claude/hooks/pretool-tool-policy.py:47-67: `_extract_targets` for Bash returns `[None] + extract_bash_write_paths(command)`. The command string itself is consumed by `extract_bash_write_paths` and discarded; only WRITE paths flow downstream to `_check_targets`. The existing `_check_targets` at line 82-92 sees only `[None, write_path1, write_path2, ...]` for Bash — it has NO access to the original command text. AC2's bash-token matcher needs to scan the original command string for tokens like 'gaode-maps/'. Without restructuring `_extract_targets` to surface the raw command (or adding a separate `_check_gaode_bash_token(command, role)` call in `main()` BEFORE `_check_targets`), the bash-token check will fail to find tokens in `cd /tmp && python3 wrapper.sh` style commands where no write paths are extracted.
objections.why_it_matters: This is a genuine implementation trap: a naive 'extend _check_targets' approach will not see the bash command string. BA's spec correctly mentions 'Bash classifier resolves first non-flag token' and 'scans the full command for gaode_denied_bash_tokens', but the technical hint to 'extend _extract_targets' implies dev will reuse the existing target-list pattern, which silently drops the command. Dev should be explicitly told to either (a) refactor _extract_targets for Bash to include the raw command as a special target type, or (b) add a separate gaode-pre-check stage in main() BEFORE the standard target loop that has access to data['tool_input']['command'].
objections.required_fix: Add a sentence to Technical Hints under 'Affected files' #2: 'For Bash, the gaode bash-token + bash-resolved-path + env-var + network-host matchers MUST receive the full command string (data[\'tool_input\'][\'command\']), NOT the WRITE-path list returned by extract_bash_write_paths(). Recommend a new pre-check stage in main() between resolve_agent_type and _check_targets: `_check_gaode_bash(role, command)` that runs all 4 bash-related gaode matchers against the raw string and exits 2 on first hit. The standard _check_targets continues unchanged for non-gaode write-path checks.'

objections.summary: Gaode-scoped fail-CLOSED preserving global LOW-10 fail-open is defensible
objections.ba_claim: BA: 'Fail-CLOSED on unresolved agent_id is gaode-scoped only; global LOW-10 fail-open posture for non-gaode tools preserved'.
objections.evidence: The asymmetric design is justified by the threat model: gaode calls are low-frequency from banned agents (currently zero — BA's invariant is 'no banned agent should ever call gaode'), so a false-deny during the dispatch race is recoverable (user re-runs). For non-gaode tools, LOW-10 documents that false-denies during dispatch race break legitimate first-write workflows — high frequency, high cost. The asymmetry correctly reflects the cost/benefit. Verified by reading /root/.claude/hooks/lib/agent_resolver.py:17-22 docstring which explicitly documents the LOW-10 contract for non-gaode tools. The hole this MIGHT leave: a banned agent that gets dispatched at the exact moment its agent-index entry is missing AND tries to call gaode would be blocked by the new fail-CLOSED; it cannot retry its way around (the agent_id remains missing for the same dispatch attempt). This is the intended behavior — the false-deny is the safer posture for gaode.
objections.why_it_matters: Positive verification. The asymmetric fail-posture is internally consistent with the documented LOW-10 contract and the spec §5.13C #5 demand for default-deny. No 'hole' is left in the gaode policy because the fail-CLOSED is universal for the gaode surface set.
objections.required_fix: No change required. Counter-positive evidence noted for transparency.
